issues.description: New branch is bolted onto keyPressEvent without restating which keys accept, dismiss, or navigate.
issues.detail: The predicate `not get_conf(...) and not key == Qt.Key_Tab` fires for every non-Tab key (arrows, Escape, modifiers) and is wedged before the existing item-guard, leaving the Enter/Return path downstream ambiguous. Restructure as a single 'is this an accept key?' predicate at the top of the handler, with the contract for each key written down.

issues.description: get_conf is called on every keystroke inside the completion popup.
issues.detail: Reading the config section on each keyPressEvent puts a dictionary walk in the typing hot path and couples the widget to the conf system. Cache the value when the popup is shown, or subscribe to option changes so the lookup happens once.

issues.description: Re-dispatching the event into textedit.keyPressEvent leaks the editor's input pipeline into the popup.
issues.detail: Calling `self.textedit.keyPressEvent(event)` after hide() reaches across the module boundary and bypasses Qt's normal propagation and any focus/proxy logic. The popup's contract should be accept / dismiss / ignore; use `event.ignore()` and let Qt deliver the key naturally.

issues.description: Awkward condition style: `not key == Qt.Key_Tab` should be `key != Qt.Key_Tab`.
issues.detail: The double-negation form mixes `not` with `==` and reads backwards. Bind the conf value to a named local and write `if not enter_accepts and key != Qt.Key_Tab:`. Trivial change, matches the surrounding code's voice.

issues.description: No test exercises the new disabled-Enter branch.
issues.detail: Completion key handling regresses silently. A single test toggling the pref off, sending Enter, and asserting no completion is accepted (plus Tab still accepts) would lock in the contract for the next maintainer.

issues.description: Option name and config-section ownership are unclear.
issues.detail: `use_enter_for_completions` is read from section 'completions' but consumed inside the editor widget, while the conf page mixes 'editor' keys nearby. A clearer name like `accept_completion_with_enter` plus a documented owner for each section would make the data shape match the UI.

synthesis.summary: The panel agrees this is a small, useful patch that solves a real user request but lands as a wart in an already-busy keyPressEvent. The core issues are taste and contract: the new branch's predicate is too broad, the Enter/Return path downstream is not cleanly short-circuited, and the popup re-dispatches the event into the editor instead of using Qt's normal propagation. Secondary issues: get_conf is called on every keystroke, the `not x == y` form should be `!=`, and there is no test. Restructure the handler around a single 'is this an accept key?' predicate, cache the conf, and add a regression test.
